goal: Close the last Review import consent hole with a fail-closed Import consent gate in ZernioBackfillWorker, and register the two Import offer analytics events #677 deferred here.
non_goals: No new derived-expiry predicate — importConsentStateSql already owns spec §5.3's derivation and this ticket only CONSUMES it.
No changes to the four enqueue-path consent gates — #677 shipped all four and they stay as-is.
No feature flag — ADR 0015 §8a R1; the backout is git revert of the PR.
No stored 'expired' value, no expiry poller, no lazy write-back — expiry stays derived on read (#670).
No change to the reactivation catch-up's non-dedup semantics — backfill_reason 'reactivation' still escapes the worker's ON CONFLICT … WHERE run_reason = 'initial'.
No touch to the section-enter-2 stagger collision between ImportOfferBanner and DashboardContent — out of the consent surface.
No CONTEXT.md or currents.md edits — those ride the post-merge documentation sweep, not this branch.
user_visible_behavior: A zernio_initial_backfill job whose business is not 'accepted' imports nothing: the outbox row completes as a skip, no Zernio API call is made, and zernio_backfill_runs is never written.

A hand-inserted zernio_initial_backfill outbox row — the admin re-enqueue path — is refused on the same predicate, making D8's 'blocked permanently, admin path included' true rather than aspirational.
An 'accepted' business still imports, including after the 7-day deadline has passed, because an answered decision outranks its deadline.
An accepted-but-never-completed run stays retryable — the guard passes and the completed_at IS NULL sentinel keeps recovery open (spec §5.1).
Admin runbook A5 no longer instructs ops to re-enqueue unconditionally; the instruction is conditioned on accepted consent and no completed initial run.
PostHog receives import_offer_created when an Import offer is minted and import_decision_recorded when an owner answers it.
invariants: Invariant #2 (transactional outbox): the guard only completes the outbox row; it enqueues nothing and writes no state outside that completion.
Invariant #8 (tenant scope): every consent read binds account_id or reaches the row by primary key from an already-tenant-scoped payload; ci:tenant-scope stays clean with no new allowlist entry.
Invariant #15 (explicit DB client): guardImportConsent takes sql: Sql as a parameter; worker/jobs/** never imports the singleton.
Spec §5.3 fail-closed: the run proceeds ONLY on import_decision = 'accepted'; declined, derived-expired and pending all no-op-complete.
Spec §5.1: declined/expired is permanent, accepted-but-incomplete stays retryable — the gate predicate is on the consent record, never on run existence.
One owner for the derivation: importConsentStateSql in src/lib/reviews/import-consent.ts stays the single spelling; guardImportConsent imports it and does not re-spell the CASE.
Postgres now(), never a JS Date — the timestamptz microsecond-truncation gotcha must not reach this boundary.
Live ingest stays structurally independent: guardImportConsent is a separate function called only by handleZernioBackfill, not a jobKind branch inside guardZernioJobEligibility.
Skip-as-success: the outbox row is completed, never failed, thrown, or retried — matching guardZernioJobEligibility's existing convention.
Analytics events are durable server facts: registered in ANALYTICS_EVENT_NAMES, not CLIENT_ENQUEUEABLE_EVENT_NAMES, and emitted inside the writing transaction.

The DB CHECK is the real registration: migration 102 must extend analytics_events_event_name_check, because a TS-allowlist-only registration rolls back every emitting transaction and ci:analytics-events does not catch it (#643 lesson, #677 D7).
edge_cases: Business row missing entirely → blocked (fail-closed), outbox completed, logged.
import_decision = 'pending' with a NULL deadline (migration 100's DEFAULT for every row) → blocked; a NULL deadline is not a live offer.
import_decision = 'pending' with a deadline in the future → blocked; consent has not been given yet, and under D9 an enqueue only exists after a Yes, so this is a hand-insert or a bug.
import_decision = 'pending' with a deadline exactly equal to now() → blocked; the boundary is inclusive (<=), a deadline that has arrived has passed.
import_decision = 'accepted' with a deadline in the past → PROCEEDS; an answered decision outranks its deadline.
backfill_reason = 'reactivation' → gated on the same 'accepted' predicate, matching archive-location-tx.ts's producer-side gate; no exemption.

Guard runs BEFORE the zernio_backfill_runs INSERT, so a refused run leaves no durable trace — deviating from spec §5.3's literal 'joins the existing pre-flight guards' wording, owner-approved 2026-08-07.
An already-completed run whose consent is now declined → still no-op-completes; the consent guard fires first and logs the block rather than the already-completed line.
createImportOffer returning 'unchanged' (idempotent re-entry) must emit NO analytics event — otherwise every dashboard mount re-mints one.
recordImportDecisionAndEnqueue returning a rejection ('already_answered' | 'expired' | 'no_offer') must emit NO analytics event.
Both event keys are business-scoped so a replayed offer or decision is dropped by ON CONFLICT (event_key) DO NOTHING rather than double-counted.
Migration 102's new list must be a strict superset of 097's, so existing analytics_events rows always re-validate under the swapped CHECK.

Deploy ordering: migration 102 must be live in a Supabase project before the emitting code reaches it, or an emission raises inside the consent transaction and rolls back a legitimate owner decision (#677 D7's hazard).

LOST-IMPORT RACE (round-1 blocking finding). An unserialized guard reads 'pending' from an in-flight hand-inserted row; the owner accepts; the acceptance transaction's NOT EXISTS sees that row still 'dispatched' and inserts no replacement; the guard then completes it as a skip. Final state is accepted consent, no completed run, and no runnable outbox row — spec §5.1's retryability violated by silent permanent data loss. The guard MUST hold the businesses row (SELECT … FOR UPDATE) inside the same sql.begin as its markOutboxCompleted, in the same business-before-outbox lock order recordImportDecisionAndEnqueue already uses.

MALFORMED-PAYLOAD CARVE-OUT (round-1 finding 5, owner-accepted with the reorder rejected). isSubscriptionTier throws at ZernioBackfillWorker.ts:135-137, BEFORE extractOutboxHandle and therefore before the consent guard. That ordering is deliberate and stays: an unparseable tier is an impossible state to assert on, not a state to branch around, and no import occurs on either path — only the outbox disposition differs (throw/retry rather than skip-complete). The consent promise 'a non-accepted job imports nothing' is unaffected; the intake's 'completes as a skip' wording applies to well-formed payloads.

A missing businesses row now exits via the consent guard, so guardZernioJobEligibility's historical backfill 'subscription_status=missing' skip line becomes unreachable for the backfill worker. Deliberate — the fail-closed reason is the more accurate one — but the existing test and both guard-ordering JSDoc blocks must be rewritten to the new authority rather than left asserting a dead branch.

rollback_plan: No feature flag (ADR 0015 §8a R1) — the backout is `git revert` of the PR. Migration 102 stays applied: its CHECK is a strict superset of 097's, so a reverted deploy simply stops emitting the two names and existing rows keep validating (097's own rollback posture). The worker guard reverts to today's un-gated behaviour, which ADR 0015 §3 already accepts while production holds zero customers (CORRECTED, round-1 miss 1: the ADR has numbered sections 1-4 and no 'R2'; R2 is spec §8a:301 and governs #677-before-#676 ordering, not this worker hole — .claude/CLAUDE.md carries the same mis-citation and should be fixed in the post-merge sweep). DEPLOY ORDER IS THE RISK, not the revert: migration 102 must be applied to the staging Supabase project before the staging ride and to the prod project in lockstep at promotion, BEFORE the emitting code is live — an emission against an un-extended CHECK raises inside the consent transaction and rolls back a legitimate owner decision (#677 D7).
observability: A structured log line from the refused guard naming the blocked consent state and business_id — the only signal that a hand-inserted or buggy enqueue was stopped, and the whole diagnostic loop for 'the import never ran'. Shaped like the existing SKIP_REASON_ARCHIVED_LOCATION line: reason + business_id, no review text.
The import_offer_created → import_decision_recorded ratio in PostHog — the offer-to-answer churn signal #677's intake named and D7 deferred here.
Queryable proof the block holds: zero zernio_backfill_runs rows for businesses whose import_decision is not 'accepted' (the guard runs before the run-row INSERT, so the absence is the assertion).
Absence of a Zernio listReviews call for a blocked business — no api_costs row, no pagination log line, so a block is distinguishable from a fetch that returned nothing.
